raw_evidence_cards.document_title: Museformer: Transformer with Fine- and Coarse-Grained Attention for Music Generation
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: The paper proposes Museformer, a Transformer with a novel fine- and coarse-grained attention for symbolic music generation, designed to model long music sequences (over 10,000 tokens) and to better generate musical repetition structures.
overlaps: Same model name Museformer
Same fine-grained attention: token of a bar attends to all tokens of most structure-relevant bars
Same coarse-grained attention: token attends to summarization of other bars to reduce computational cost
Same combination rationale: capture music structure-related correlations plus other contextual information
Same setting: symbolic music generation with long sequences
differences: The abstract does not specify the exact bar-selection mechanism beyond 'selected via similarity statistics' (e.g., the previous 1st, 2nd, 4th and 8th bars), which is a detail not fully elaborated in the retrieved abstract text

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: MusicExtender: Generating Polyphonic Piano Music with Long-term Structures via Similarity-guided Diffusion Inpainting
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: MusicExtender is a diffusion-based model for polyphonic piano music generation with long-term structures, using a similarity-based phrase-level structure annotation and a phrase-level autoregressive diffusion-inpainting paradigm.
overlaps: Addresses long-term musical structure modeling in music generation
Uses bar-/phrase-level structure and similarity computation
differences: Uses a diffusion model with inpainting rather than a Transformer with fine-/coarse-grained attention
Focuses on polyphonic piano roll representation and phrase-level autoregressive generation
Does not describe fine-grained or coarse-grained attention mechanisms

raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: Introduces a generic similarity-based annotation method to annotate musical structures at the phrase level, and a diffusion-inpainting generation model (MusicExtender) that generates polyphonic piano music under external structural conditions, with a structural regularization term.
overlaps: Uses similarity computation to determine structure-related musical units (bar/phrase level).
Uses the derived structural information to guide a downstream neural model.

Focus is symbolic polyphonic piano generation, not attention-based structure modeling.

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: Self-Similarity-Based and Novelty-based loss for music structure analysis
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: Proposes a supervised deep-learning approach for music structure analysis (MSA) that jointly learns an encoder whose features yield a self-similarity matrix (SSM) approximating a ground-truth SSM (SSM-loss) and learns convolution kernels that produce a novelty score from the estimated SSM (novelty-loss); also introduces self-attention layers to learn track-relative features.
overlaps: Uses similarity statistics (self-similarity matrix) to explore and represent the repetition/homogeneity structure of music.
Employs an attention mechanism (self-attention) within a music-structure model.
differences: Attention is used for track-relative feature learning, not to restrict fine-grained attention to a set of structure-related bars.
The output is segment boundary detection / novelty score, not a selection of structure-related bars (e.g., 1st, 2nd, 4th, 8th bars) to guide attention.
No bar-level selection mechanism derived from similarity statistics is described.

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: Enhancing long-term structure in symbolic music generation via a cascaded Skeleton-to-texture framework
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: CAST is a framework for long-range symbolic music generation based on explicit skeleton guidance, decoupling generation into macro-harmonic planning and micro-texture filling. It uses MusicBERT to extract semantic skeletons and cross-attention to map them to a MuseFormer generator, and explicitly selects MuseFormer as the baseline because it represents the state-of-the-art in sparse attention mechanisms.
overlaps: Characterizes MuseFormer as the state-of-the-art in sparse attention mechanisms and uses it as the baseline generator, indicating the sparse-attention efficiency mechanism is treated as established prior art by later work.
differences: CAST's own contribution is explicit structural skeleton guidance and cross-attention mapping, not the blocksparse/efficiency mechanism itself; it does not claim a new sparse-attention or blocksparse encoding technique.

sources.title: Enhancing long-term structure in symbolic music generation via a cascaded Skeleton-to-texture framework
sources.quote: For validation, we selected MuseFormer, which represents the state-of-the-art in sparse attention mechanisms, as the baseline model.
